output.brief:
The rejects come from an interaction. Arnholt resin arrives wetter (0.27–0.33% at the dryer inlet) than Quillan (0.11–0.14%). Dryer D5 is degraded, with a dew point of about −16 to −19 °C against −40 °C. D5 can still dry Quillan acceptably, but it cannot dry Arnholt to the 0.20% limit.

- Arnholt in D5 on Press 5 had about 10% rejects.
- Arnholt on Press 7, whose dryer D7 is healthy, had 0.8%.
- Quillan in D5 had 0.9%.
- Arnholt lot A-2291 dried in a −40 °C portable dryer and fed to Press 5 gave 0.8% rejects, against 10.4% through D5 the day before.

The new operators are not the cause. Their reject rate matches the experienced operators' on both resins. The second shift looks worse only because all its VX runs on Press 5. Do not put them on performance plans.

This week, repair D5 and restore its original alarm limit. Keep Arnholt off D5 until D5 is verified at −40 °C. Add a moisture check at the press feed throat for every resin lot. Routing Arnholt to Press 7 alone would stop the rejects but leave D5 broken.

One gap remains. Arnholt was stored in the north annex and Quillan in the main warehouse, so storage and supplier are confounded. Ask Arnholt for the wetness at shipment, and hold off on moving the octabins until that is known.
